question_text: What does 'TRANSPARENT' mean in a government context?

hint_ladder.title: Isipin ang Malinaw na Bintana
hint_ladder.text: Isipin mo ang isang malinaw na bintana—walang nakaharang, kita lahat. 'Yan ang literal ng 'transparent'. Sa gobyerno, pareho: bukas, walang tinatago.

hint_ladder.title: Ang Government Twist
hint_ladder.text: Sa gobyerno, transparent means nakikita ng mamamayan ang decisions at pondo. Hindi nakatago, accountable ang officials.

hint_ladder.title: Spot the Opposites
hint_ladder.text: Tatlo sa choices ang kabaligtaran—secretive, hidden, confusing. Alisin mo ang mga antonym, ang matitira ay tamang sagot.

hint_ladder.title: The Final Clue
hint_ladder.text: Ang tamang sagot ay pinagsamang 'open' at 'accountable.' Bukas para makita ng tao, at accountable para may pananagutan.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you confused 'transparent' with its antonym 'secretive.' But transparent means open, not secretive.

B.text: You might have chosen B because 'hidden' seems similar to 'not seen,' but transparent means openly seen, not concealed.

C.text: Correct. In government, transparent means open and accountable—everything is visible and officials are answerable.

D.text: You might have chosen D because 'confusing' sounds like not clear, but transparent actually means crystal clear and easy to understand.

next_time_rule: Remember: transparent sa gobyerno = open and accountable. Mental trick: 'see-through' governance—kita ng tao ang lahat, may pananagutan.
